lines: Solim: takes up to eight note voltages, folds each one by octaves into the range between two limits, and then sorts them
One of the voltages to be limited and sorted; an unpatched jack is skipped rather than read as 0V
A limited and sorted voltage; the results fill the outputs from the first one down, with no gaps
Sets the lower limit, -5V to 5V, shown on the display as the note it rounds down to
Sets the upper limit, -5V to 5V, shown on the display as the note it rounds down to
Sorts the results into ascending or descending order, or leaves them in input order, marked ASC, NONE and DESC
Replaces the lower limit knob while it is patched, clamped to -5V to 5V
Replaces the upper limit knob while it is patched, clamped to -5V to 5V
Replaces the sort switch while it is patched: a positive voltage sorts ascending, a negative one descending, and 0V sorts nothing
Menu — Process at audio rate — processes every sample instead of about 6000 times a second
Menu — Polyphonic output — sends all the results down the first output as channels and leaves the other seven at 0V
Note — a single polyphonic cable on one input is read as up to eight separate values, one per channel; as soon as two inputs are patched, every input is read as its first channel only
Note — limiting is done by adding or subtracting whole volts, so a note keeps its name and only changes octave; nothing is quantized
Note — the lower limit is applied first and the upper limit second, so limits less than 1V apart, or an upper limit below the lower one, can leave a result below the lower limit
Note — expanders chain outward from this module: SL-I and the Input Octaver to the left, SL-O and the Output Octaver to the right, and SL-R on either side
Note — the small green lamp beside an output lights while a value is being sent to it
